title: Graded triangular decomposition of a generalized Serre quotient
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set and $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ an integer matrix such that $a_{ii}=2$, $a_{ij}\leq0$ for $i
e j$, and $a_{ij}=0$ if and only if $a_{ji}=0$. In the category of rational Lie algebras [def-wf-lie-algebra], let $L(A)$ be the free Lie algebra on symbols $H_i,E_i,F_i$ modulo the Lie ideal generated by
$$[H_i,H_j],\quad [E_i,F_j]-\delta_{ij}H_i,\quad [H_i,E_j]-a_{ij}E_j,\quad [H_i,F_j]+a_{ij}F_j,$$
and $(\operatorname{ad}E_i)^{1-a_{ij}}E_j$, $(\operatorname{ad}F_i)^{1-a_{ij}}F_j$ for $i
e j$. A free Lie algebra means the Lie algebra with the universal property that an arbitrary assignment of its generators to a rational Lie algebra extends uniquely to a Lie homomorphism. Write $\varepsilon_i$ for the standard basis of $\mathbf Z^I$. The assignments $\deg H_i=0$, $\deg E_i=\varepsilon_i$, $\deg F_i=-\varepsilon_i$ give a direct-sum grading $L(A)= igoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z^I}L(A)_m$, with $[L(A)_m,L(A)_n]\subseteq L(A)_{m+n}$. The map $\mathbf Q^I	o L(A)_0$, $(q_i)\mapsto\sum_iq_iH_i$, is an isomorphism. If $L(A)_m
e0$ and $m
e0$, then $m$ has either all coordinates nonnegative or all coordinates nonpositive. More precisely, the subalgebra generated by the $E_i$ is the free Lie algebra on the $E_i$ modulo the ideal generated solely by the positive Serre relations $(\operatorname{ad}E_i)^{1-a_{ij}}E_j$; the analogous assertion holds for the $F_i$, and these two subalgebras and $ igoplus_i\mathbf QH_i$ form a vector-space direct sum equal to $L(A)$. In particular $L(A)_{\varepsilon_i}=\mathbf QE_i
e0$, $L(A)_{-\varepsilon_i}=\mathbf QF_i
e0$, and $L(A)_{n\varepsilon_i}=0$ for every integer $n$ with $|n|>1$. No finite-type or nonsingularity assumption on $A$ is imposed. For $I=\varnothing$ all spaces are zero.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504: Weyl-relations triangular decomposition and passage to the positive and negative Serre ideals; p.508, characteristic-zero extension. The details referred there to Bourbaki VIII §4 no.2 and Serre VI are WANTED; this node isolates the graded quotient theorem, not finite-dimensional root-system realization.

proof.text: First impose only the four Weyl families of relations and call the resulting algebra $W=W(A)$. By [lem-sfb-weyl-relations-free-normal-form], its subalgebras $\mathfrak n^+$ and $\mathfrak n^-$ generated by $E_i$ and $F_i$ are free on those generators, the $H_i$ are independent, and $W=\mathfrak n^-\oplus\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ as vector spaces, where $\mathfrak h=\bigoplus_i\mathbf QH_i$. This applies to $A$ regarded as a rational matrix, including a singular matrix. Let $N_{ij}=1-a_{ij}\ge1$ and $s_{ij}^+=(\operatorname{ad}E_i)^{N_{ij}}E_j$ for $i\ne j$. Let $K^+$ be the ideal generated by these elements inside $\mathfrak n^+$, and define $K^-$ inside $\mathfrak n^-$ with $E$ replaced by $F$. The ideal of $W$ generated by both families is denoted $J$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-free-lie-homogeneous-presentation-grading] to the free Lie algebra on $H_i,E_i,F_i$, with degrees $0,\varepsilon_i,-\varepsilon_i$ in $\mathbf Z^I$. Each Weyl relation is homogeneous: the only potentially nonzero correction term in $[E_i,F_j]-\delta_{ij}H_i$ occurs for $i=j$, when its degree is zero. The other three families have degrees $0$, $\varepsilon_j$, and $-\varepsilon_j$. Each Serre element has degree $N_{ij}\varepsilon_i+\varepsilon_j$ or its negative. Thus both $W$ and $L(A)$ have direct-sum gradings with the claimed bracket rule. The map $W\to L(A)$ preserves degree. Apply the same lemma to the free algebras $\mathfrak n^\pm$ and their Serre ideals: $K^\pm$ are homogeneous for the multidegrees of their generators. Under the injections of step 1 these gradings agree with the grading of $W$, since every bracket word has the same degree in either construction.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text:
We compute the brackets of a positive Serre generator with the opposite simple generators using the Weyl relations of [lem-sfb-weyl-relations-free-normal-form] and Jacobi [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Fix $i\ne j$, put $D=\operatorname{ad}E_i$ and $a=a_{ij}$. Induction gives $[H_i,D^rE_j]=(a+2r)D^rE_j$. Also $[F_i,E_j]=0$, and Jacobi gives $[F_i,Dv]=D[F_i,v]-[H_i,v]$. Starting at $r=0$, this proves
$$[F_i,D^rE_j]=-r(a+r-1)D^{r-1}E_j\quad(r\ge1):$$
the coefficient at the next stage is $-r(a+r-1)-(a+2r)=-(r+1)(a+r)$. It is zero at $r=N_{ij}=1-a$. For $k\notin\{i,j\}$ the bracket $[F_k,D^rE_j]$ is zero by induction because $[F_k,E_i]=[F_k,E_j]=0$. Finally $[F_j,D^{N_{ij}}E_j]=-D^{N_{ij}}H_j$. Here $DH_j=-a_{ji}E_i$ and $D^2H_j=0$. If $N_{ij}\ge2$ this vanishes, and if $N_{ij}=1$ then $a_{ij}=0$, so the assumed symmetric zero pattern gives $a_{ji}=0$. Consequently $[F_k,s_{ij}^+]=0$ for every $k$. The same derivation identity gives
$$[H_k,s_{ij}^+]=(N_{ij}a_{ki}+a_{kj})s_{ij}^+.$$
This calculation uses no inverse of $A$ and no root-system realization.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text:
We now show that $K^+$ is an ideal of all of $W$, rather than only of $\mathfrak n^+$. Write $V$ for the span of the elements $\operatorname{ad}(E_{l_1})\cdots\operatorname{ad}(E_{l_r})s_{ij}^+$ with $r\ge0$. It is contained in $K^+$ and stable under every $\operatorname{ad}(E_l)$; Jacobi then proves stability under brackets of $E_l$ by induction on bracket words. Hence it is an ideal of $\mathfrak n^+$ containing the $s_{ij}^+$, so $V=K^+$. Each displayed vector is an eigenvector for $\operatorname{ad}(H_k)$: Jacobi adds $a_{kl}$ when a bracket with $E_l$ is prepended to a weight vector, starting with the last formula of step 3. Thus $[H_k,K^+]\subseteq K^+$. Prove $[F_k,V]\subseteq V$ by induction on $r$. The base is step 3; the induction step is the explicit identity
$$[F_k,[E_l,u]]=-\delta_{kl}[H_k,u]+[E_l,[F_k,u]].$$
Both terms lie in $V$ by the already proved Cartan stability and the induction hypothesis. This proves stability under all three types of generators. Another bracket-word induction using Jacobi proves $[W,K^+]\subseteq K^+$. All Lie-ideal and derivation manipulations here are direct uses of [def-wf-lie-algebra]; the ambient generators and their relations are those of [lem-sfb-weyl-relations-free-normal-form].

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text: The assignment $\theta(H_i)=-H_i$, $\theta(E_i)=F_i$, $\theta(F_i)=E_i$ preserves all four Weyl relations of [lem-sfb-weyl-relations-free-normal-form]. For example $[F_i,E_j]=-\delta_{ij}H_i=\delta_{ij}\theta(H_i)$ and $[-H_i,F_j]=a_{ij}F_j$; the fourth relation is checked in the same way. The free universal property and the definition of quotient therefore extend this assignment to a Lie endomorphism of $W$; its square fixes every generator, hence is the identity. It exchanges the two free subalgebras and the two Serre families, so it sends $K^+$ to $K^-$. Applying it to step 4 proves that $K^-$ is an ideal of $W$. Therefore $K^++K^-$ is an ideal of $W$ containing both Serre families, so $J\subseteq K^++K^-$. Conversely $J$ contains every bracket of a positive or negative generator with its corresponding Serre family, hence contains $K^+$ and $K^-$. Thus $J=K^+\oplus K^-$, the sum being direct by step 1.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text:
The presentation identifies $L(A)$ with $W/J$: both quotients have the same generators and impose exactly the Weyl and Serre relations, so their universal homomorphisms fixing the generators are inverse. By steps 1 and 5, the map
$$(\mathfrak n^-/K^-)\oplus\mathfrak h\oplus(\mathfrak n^+/K^+)\longrightarrow W/J$$
is a vector-space isomorphism. Explicitly, it sends a triple of classes to the class of their sum; it is surjective by the decomposition of $W$, and a sum belongs to $J=K^-\oplus K^+$ exactly when its Cartan component is zero and its two other components lie in their respective $K^\pm$. This proves injectivity and well-definedness without a splitting choice. In particular the positive summand is the subalgebra generated by the images of the $E_i$ and is the free Lie algebra modulo only its positive Serre ideal; the negative assertion is identical. This is a vector-space direct sum, not a claim that brackets between the three summands are zero.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, first proof, printed p.504; the explicit Serre-ideal and grading arguments below are supplied by the agent, with the corrected Weyl/Serre conventions of the item.

proof.text: Finish degree by degree using [lem-sfb-free-lie-homogeneous-presentation-grading] and the isomorphism in step 6. Each nonempty positive bracket word has degree in $\mathbf N^I\setminus\{0\}$; each negative word has degree in its negative. The maps in step 6 preserve degrees, so all nonzero components outside degree zero lie in one of these two cones, and the zero component is precisely the surviving independent Cartan space. Hence $(q_i)\mapsto\sum_iq_iH_i$ identifies $\mathbf Q^I$ with $L(A)_0$. The degree $\varepsilon_i$ part of a free positive algebra is spanned just by $E_i$, and this vector is nonzero: the free universal map to the one-dimensional abelian rational Lie algebra sending $E_i$ to $1$ and the other generators to zero detects it. Every generator of $K^+$ has total degree $N_{ij}+1\ge2$; bracketing with positive words only increases total degree. The explicit ideal-span assertion of the grading lemma thus gives $(K^+)_{\varepsilon_i}=0$. Consequently $L(A)_{\varepsilon_i}=\mathbf QE_i\ne0$; apply $\theta$ for $-\varepsilon_i$. For $n>1$ a positive word of degree $n\varepsilon_i$ contains only $E_i$. Every such word is zero: a length-two word is $[E_i,E_i]=0$, and for any longer fully bracketed word one of its two factors has length at least two, so induction kills that factor. Therefore $L(A)_{n\varepsilon_i}=0$ for $n>1$, and $\theta$ handles $n<-1$. For $I=\varnothing$ all free generating sets and the Cartan basis are empty, so every space is zero.
